name: Окно «Спуск»: фон каждого биома — место и его обитатели, что ждут отряд, на одном арте (слова автора 30.09.2026: «сам задний фон каждого биома именно в окне спуска нужно сделать как задний фон, а не как заглушку в виде арены, — арена должна быть на экране боёвки, а сам задний фон показывается и как бы обитатели, которые нас условно ждут, исходя по лору, задним фоном на 1 арте»). Четыре биома прототипа: Мастерская форм, Подземный лес, Библиотека Улариона, Искусственный Стоун-Хейм. Способ — «Глубокий промт» (art/style/style.md), перенесённый на сцену: место · кто ждёт, от ближнего к дальнему, — облик, характер в позе и детали из записей сказителя · свет · кадр. Кадр 21:9 под вёрстку окна screens/descent.js: слева — выбор биома, слева сверху — название и цитата, снизу — состояние и кнопки; поэтому левая четверть и низ — тень, фигуры и самый яркий свет — в правых двух третях. Обитатели — фигуры в глубине сцены, а не ряд портретов; к запросу приложены два референса стиля и три портрета обитателей биома (design/ui/assets/art/foes/) — только ради облика. Лор — docs/lore/мастерская-форм-текст.md, docs/content/враги-биомов.md (разделы 2–4), docs/lore/дайджест.md. Без спойлеров §38 GDD и раздела дайджеста «Нельзя показывать раннему игроку»: ни искажённых, ни нежити, ни Этриона. Выгрузка — design/ui/assets/art/descent/<биом>.jpg, 1688×716, строки в tools/art-gen/ui-art.json.
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic key art of a legendary place with a sense of great scale and depth. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals, cracks, glowing plants, lava — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes, spores, sparks and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no runes that look like letters, no real-world scripts: tablets, slabs, cylinders, banners and walls carry no writing at all — only blank surfaces or long straight parallel grooves. No watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. No occult symbols, no pentagrams. No gore, no blood, no skulls, no bones, no corpses, no undead, no twisted or distorted creatures, no demons. No purple, no violet, no magenta light. No heroes, no adventurers, no people from the surface world — only the inhabitants of this place. Not a lineup of portraits, no close-up faces, no figure taller than a third of the picture except the giants in the depth. Not a mannequin, not a crash-test dummy, not a marionette on strings: no stiff, passive, awkward or doll-like poses, no dead or empty eyes.

descent-bg.frame: Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: wide cinematic panorama, 21:9, painted edge to edge over the whole frame — no black bars at the top or bottom, no letterbox, no dark border — the full-screen background of the game's Descent window, where the player chooses a place under the city of Endalor and sends a squad of heroes down. The picture shows one place of the Descent and the inhabitants who are waiting for the heroes, as an old storyteller would describe them. The viewer stands at the entrance and looks into the depth; the inhabitants stand in the middle distance and in the depth, turned toward the viewer, calm and dangerous, as if they already know someone is coming. They belong to the scene: full figures at their distance, silhouettes lit from below with a rim of light, the largest and most important ones far away in the depth — never a row of portraits, never a close-up. The game lays its interface over the picture, so the composition leaves room for it: the left quarter of the picture is dark and calm — a near wall, trunks or stacks in deep shadow, no figures and no bright light there; the upper left, from the left quarter to the middle, is a calm dark vault, canopy or haze without figures — the game writes the name of the place there; the bottom fifth falls into shadow — dark floor, no faces there. The path or hall leads into the depth toward a vanishing point at about 60% of the width and 45% of the height; all figures and the brightest light sit in the right two thirds of the picture, between 15% and 80% of the height. Atmospheric depth, haze, a few strong light sources rising from below. Mood: awe, quiet menace, an invitation to go down. Pathos: the inhabitants are worthy and dangerous enemies — alive, proud, each with a character in the posture — not mannequins, not statues on display. The first two attached images are style references only: take their brushwork, light and color handling, not their subjects or composition. The other attached images are portraits of some of the inhabitants of this place: keep their look — body, material, face, clothing and tools — but paint them small, as full figures standing in the scene at their distance and turned toward the viewer; do not copy the portraits' framing, crop or pose.

jobs.subject: Subject: the Workshop of Forms (air, the god Vial), the first hall under Endalor. The place: a hall so huge that its vault is lost in darkness and its walls in haze; here the god once sculpted living beings from clay before giving them to the world above, and the work was left in the middle. Bodies come out of the walls half-sculpted — an arm without a hand, a back without a face, a beast with only one half made. Heavy wooden worktables stand in rows with unfinished clay works, sculpting chisels and clay-stained cloths. Pale sand is everywhere: it lies in drifts between the tables, falls from cracks in the vault in thin streams, and in places stands as a column of falling sand from floor to vault, like an hourglass no one turns. Light: white-green crystals grow in the cracks of the floor and walls and glow from within, like a candle left in each, and throw a cold halo upward; the only warm color in the hall is the ochre clay. The silence of a workshop abandoned in the middle of the day. Nothing is ugly: every body is made precisely and calmly, just not finished. Who waits here, from near to far: (1) in the middle distance, between the worktables, never in the foreground and each no taller than a quarter of the picture, three unfinished elves of grey-green clay stand turned toward the viewer — the Faceless one, a slender elf-shaped figure in a sketch of clothing with a rope for a belt, holding a stone blank of a sword without a guard; his smooth face has only two shallow thumb marks where the eyes should be, and still he looks straight at you; the Long-armed one, thin and stooped, whose one arm reaches almost to the floor and ends in a heavy stone hand; the Hollow one, whose chest is open like an empty mold, his head thrown back, a thin whirl of sand and air leaving his chest; (2) at a table in the middle distance on the right, two servants in clay aprons who still keep working — a thickset apprentice with forearms twice as thick as they should be, kneading a lump of clay, and a tall stooped carver whose right hand is a fan of thin blades — both have raised their heads and look at the viewer; (3) far in the depth, towering over the last tables, the First Sketch — a hunched giant three times the height of a man, so even far away he stands three times taller than the elves near the viewer and his head reaches the haze under the vault, made of two halves that do not match: the left half an elf, the right half a beast with clay fur, a clawed paw and a beast's leg; instead of a face a smooth mask with two hollows; a small foreign hand is stuck on his side; he is trying a clay part against his own body; (4) at the very end of the hall, in front of a tall dark passage that glows faintly white-green and leads deeper down, stands the Master — the only finished one: a tall slender elf of smooth polished clay with long hair and a calm face, eyes closed, a master's apron, wrapped forearms, a chisel of glowing white-green stone at his belt, one hand raised palm forward: stop. He is small with distance but clearly readable against the light of the passage. Composition: the path between the worktables leads from the bottom of the picture to the Master and the glowing passage; the First Sketch looms in the haze just before it; columns of falling sand stand on both sides of the path; the left quarter is the near wall of the hall in deep shadow — no figure stands there, only the faint relief of a half-sculpted body in the stone; the upper left is dark vault; the bottom of the picture is dark floor with drifts of sand, empty of figures.

jobs.subject: Subject: the Underground Forest (air, the god Vial) — his finished creation: what was left half-done in the Workshop of Forms is completed here. The place: a forest without a sun, deep underground. Tall pale trunks, smooth and bone-white like birches, rise into darkness; their roots drink white-green crystal light from glowing veins in the ground, and their leaves and moss glow faintly white-green from within. The air is thick: glowing spores and pollen hang and drift in it. Pale moss, roots and fallen trunks with the bark peeled off in even strips cover the ground. A narrow hunters' path winds between the trunks into the depth. Who waits here, from near to far: (1) the huntsmen — finished elves with calm, attentive faces, skin as pale as the trunks, jackets woven of bast and bark — stand among the trunks on both sides of the path, short bows lowered, arrows on the string, and watch the viewer; the tallest of them, the Elder Huntsman, has the gaze of a shepherd, not of a hunter, and a bone horn on a strap across his chest; (2) a pack of pale wolves the size of calves, their fur as pale as the trunks, crouch in the undergrowth around the path, their eyes reflecting white-green light; (3) a large pale lynx with glowing white-green ear tufts lies along a low branch above the path, ready to jump; (4) a huge forest aurochs, taller than a man, with moss and small glowing mushrooms on its horns, stands half-hidden among the trunks; (5) far in the depth, in a clearing full of light, lies the Mother of the Pack — a she-beast the size of a house, quiet and enormous, with a wolf's build, a bear's shoulders and a lynx's ear tufts; her pale mane glows white-green along her spine; a wolf cub sits between her front paws; she has raised her head and looks at the viewer; (6) behind her, where the path goes deeper down, a tall column of whirling leaves, spores and glowing pollen turns slowly — it keeps its shape only while it moves, and for a moment it seems to hold the faint outline of a figure with a bow. Composition: the viewer stands at the edge of the forest; the path recedes to the clearing with the Mother of the Pack and the whirling column; the left quarter is near trunks and roots in deep shadow; the upper left is dark canopy; the bottom of the picture is dark roots and moss.

jobs.subject: Subject: the Library of Ularion (earth, the god Ularion) — the workshop of the god of knowledge, a real ancient library cut in dark stone deep underground. The place: halls step down and down; tall stone stacks hold stone tablets and stone cylinders covered with long straight parallel engraved grooves, like ruled lines with nothing written between them; on long stone worktables parts of dwarves and of mechanisms lie together — stone arms and hands, bronze hinges, gears — because the god made the people and the machine with the same hands; an hourglass with glowing amber sand stands at every workplace. Light: amber — from glowing amber crystals in the cracks of the floor, from the sand of the hourglasses and from the grooves of the tablets; the vault is in deep shadow. Who waits here, from near to far: (1) dwarf-puppets carved of dark grey stone and bronze, with bronze hinges at the elbows and knees — short and enormously broad, barrel chests, thick short necks, broad faces, braided stone beards — stand between the stacks and at the tables, turned toward the viewer; one holds his arms straight like a column and has no hinges at all, one has arms that unfold like a folding ruler, one leaks dark oil from every joint and holds an oil can; their amber eyes are alive and fixed on the viewer with purpose — only the writing they cannot understand; (2) stone beetles the size of chests crawl on the floor and on the shelves, amber light glowing along the seams of their shells; one beetle the size of a cart grinds a tablet with its jaws, and stone dust falls from it; (3) a swarm of whispering stone grit hangs over a table in the rough shape of a figure, crumbling and gathering again; (4) far in the depth, taller than the stacks, stands the Keeper — the first mechanism of the world: a colossal bronze apparatus on long knee-jointed legs like a giant crab's, its bronze housing open at the chest where great gears turn around the oldest, darkest gear glowing amber, a single great round amber lens under a heavy bronze brow instead of a face, its beam sweeping the rows; (5) at the very end of the hall, at the top of steps that lead deeper down, stands the Seer — the only finished dwarf of the Library, carved of smooth stone, with a calm face, holding an open stone tablet whose grooves glow amber as he reads. Composition: the viewer stands at the top of the stairs into the hall; the rows of stacks recede to the Keeper and the Seer; the left quarter is a near stack in deep shadow; the upper left is dark vault; the bottom of the picture is dark stone floor.

jobs.subject: Subject: the Artificial Stone-Heim (earth, the god Ularion) — his finished creation: a full-size living copy of the dwarven city Stone-Heim, deep underground. The place: a vast cavern with a city on its walls in tiers and ledges; bridges and trestles cross the void, lift cages hang on long chains, rails run along the ledges; forges and foundries glow, hammers ring, lava runs in stone channels. For a thousand years everything here has worked without dispute and without error. Light: warm amber and orange from the lava channels, the forges and the amber crystal the forges burn; it lights the stone from below; steam, smoke and sparks rise; the vault is in deep shadow. Who waits here, from near to far: (1) on a wide stone bridge that leads into the city, dwarves of smooth warm stone — finished, not puppets: short and enormously broad, barrel chests, thick short necks, broad faces, braided beards — stand in a calm, orderly crowd turned toward the viewer, each with the tool of his craft: a miner in a leather helmet with a pickaxe, a riveter with tongs and a belt of red-hot rivets, a hammer-smith with a great hammer on his shoulder, a chain-man with a lifting chain wound around his arm, a channel-keeper with a long hook over the lava, sparks in his beard; they do not hurry and do not argue; (2) a heavy draft lizard in a collar worn to a shine stands harnessed to a mine wagon; (3) a piece of paving stone has stood up on thick legs, amber light glowing in the seams between its stones; (4) far in the depth, on a raised square at the end of the bridge, stands the Head of the City — a dwarf no taller than the others, in a heavy caftan with a chain of office, a hollow amber crown glowing on his head, one hand raised in a calm order; the whole quarter stands behind him; (5) beyond the square, in the haze over the void, looms a giant figure of rough stone with glowing amber veins, in the outline of a wanderer with a staff — as if the rock itself has just noticed itself. Composition: the viewer stands at the start of the bridge; the bridge and the crowd recede to the Head of the City and the giant in the haze; tiers with glowing forges and lift cages rise on the far wall of the cavern; the left quarter is the near cavern wall in deep shadow; the upper left is dark vault with a few hanging chains; the bottom of the picture is the dark stone of the bridge.
